title: Cohort Cascade Replay Runbook — prototype for staged rollouts and emergency rewind
creator: Maya Patel
description: Prototype flows and annotated screens for a 'Cohort Cascade Replay' runbook in Redwood Console. The goal is to give operators an interactive rehearsal and emergency-rewind experience for staged rollouts (canary, A/B, cohort fades) that combines timeline replay, per-cohort metrics playback, and one-click evacuation or rewind actions. This ticket captures the prototype scope, design rationale, acceptance criteria, and feedback from the March 10th design review.
goals: Create a compact timeline scrubber that replays traffic changes and metric deltas per cohort
Expose an operator-first emergency 'evacuate cohort' action with clear safe-guards and undo path
Surface cost delta and latency impact for each step so teams can balance safety vs spend during rollouts
Provide a rehearsal mode that simulates rollback paths and expected traffic re-distribution before applying to prod
anchors: Timeline scrubber (0:00 -> current): shows cohort shifts, request volumes, and key metric overlays (latency, error %)
Cohort card stack: per-cohort snapshots with sample requests, attribution to release variant, and cost impact
Rewind/evacuate control with two-step confirmation and optional dry-run simulation
Runbook panel with suggested mitigations, linked playbooks and linked incident timelines
acceptance_criteria: Prototype screens for timeline scrubber + cohort stack are present in Figma and linked above
Interactive prototype allows a reviewer to scrub to any step and see per-cohort metric snapshots
Evacuate action includes a dry-run simulation that visualizes expected traffic distribution and cost delta
Design review feedback items are captured and an implementation handoff doc is started for engineering
decisions: We will use a single timeline view combining metric overlays rather than separate per-cohort timelines to reduce cognitive load.
Evacuate will be implemented as a prioritized traffic-swap to a stable variant + gradual fade out, with an immediate stop option only for critical incidents.
Cost delta will show estimated per-minute spend change and cumulative spend over selected rewind window; we will avoid showing absolute billing numbers until finance validates estimates.
Accessibility: scrubber will support keyboard shortcuts and a high-contrast collapsed mode; charts will include text summaries for screen readers.
tradeoffs: Combining metrics on a single timeline simplifies scanning but risks occluding small-signal regressions — mitigated by a tappable metric selection filter.
Providing a visible immediate-stop button increases risk of operator error; two-step confirmation and telemetry gating reduces accidental use but slightly increases time-to-mitigation.
Simulated dry-run accuracy will be probabilistic; we prioritize clarity of expected direction rather than exact token-level cost estimation.
implementation_notes: Engineering to build a lightweight playback API that returns cohort-level metrics by timestamp window. Prototype uses mocked data stored in Drive.
Console should persist safety choices per-project (e.g., forbid immediate-stop for some orgs). Add RBAC check during implementation.
Add telemetry events: replay_started, replay_scrubbed_to, evacuate_dryrun_viewed, evacuate_executed, evacuate_undone
